Juice = \(\frac{\text{Part of juice}}{\text{Total parts}}\) × Total mixture

questions.question: On whose recommendation was the Central Vigilance Commission established?
questions.questionHtml: On whose recommendation was the Central Vigilance Commission established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Santhanam Committee

Key Points

  • The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was established on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee.
  • The Santhanam Committee, also known as the Committee on Prevention of Corruption, was set up in 1962 to address issues related to corruption in India.
  • The Committee was headed by K. Santhanam, a prominent Indian politician and freedom fighter.
  • The CVC was created in 1964 to act as an apex vigilance institution, free of control from any executive authority, monitoring all vigilance activity under the Central Government and advising various authorities in central Government organizations in planning, executing, reviewing, and reforming their vigilance work.

Additional Information

  • The Central Vigilance Commission was conferred statutory status by the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.
  • The primary function of the CVC is to address governmental corruption and ensure integrity in public administration.
  • The CVC is not subject to the control of any executive authority, thereby ensuring its independence and impartiality.
  • It has the power to inquire or cause inquiries into offenses alleged to have been committed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 by certain categories of public servants.
  • The CVC also undertakes or causes an inquiry into complaints received under the Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers' Resolution (PIDPI), which is also known as the Whistleblower Protection Resolution.

questions.question: The force exerted on a body by the virtue of acceleration of gravity acting on the body is called:
questions.questionHtml: The force exerted on a body by the virtue of acceleration of gravity acting on the body is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Weight.

Key Points

Concept:

  • Falling Freely: Freefall is the motion of a body where it weight is the only force acting on an object.
    • The acceleration of free-falling objects is called the acceleration due to gravity since objects are pulled towards the centre of the earth.
    • Weight: It is a measure of the force of gravity acting on a body.

The formula for weight is given by

w = mg 

  • As weight is a force its SI unit is also the same as that of force, the SI unit of weight is Newton (N).
  • Weight depends upon the mass and the acceleration due to gravity, the mass may not change but the acceleration due to gravity changes from place to place.

Explanation:

  • The acceleration due to gravity is constant on the surface of the Earth and has a value of 9.8 m/s2.
  • The force acting on the body due to acceleration due to gravity is weight.

So, The acceleration due to gravity acting on a body is called weight.

Additional Information

  • A microphone receives the sound signal and converts it into electrical signals.

questions.question: The cost of a house is Rs. 40,000 and that of household articles is Rs. 15,000. If the rate of premium for fire insurance is 7.5%, then what will be the fire insurance premium for an amount of 80% of the total value of the house and articles?
questions.questionHtml: The cost of a house is Rs. 40,000 and that of household articles is Rs. 15,000. If the rate of premium for fire insurance is 7.5%, then what will be the fire insurance premium for an amount of 80% of the total value of the house and articles?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total value of assets = 40000 + 15000 = 55000

Effective premium rate on total value = 7.5% of 80%

⇒ Effective rate = (7.5 × 80) ÷ 100 = 6%

⇒ Total Premium = 6% of 55000 = (6 ÷ 100) × 55000 = 3300

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,300.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of house = Rs. 40,000

Cost of household articles = Rs. 15,000

Rate of premium = 7.5%

Insured coverage = 80% of total value

Calculations:

⇒ Total value of house and articles = 40,000 + 15,000 = Rs. 55,000

⇒ Insured amount = 80% of total value

⇒ Insured amount = (80 ÷ 100) × 55,000 = Rs. 44,000

⇒ Fire insurance premium = 7.5% of insured amount

⇒ Premium = (7.5 ÷ 100) × 44,000

⇒ Premium = 7.5 × 440 = Rs. 3,300

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,300.

Additional Information

Percentage Calculation

To find X% of Y, use the formula: (X ÷ 100) × Y. This fundamental concept is widely used to calculate premiums, discounts, and simple interest.

Successive Percentages

When applying consecutive percentages (like taking A% of B% of a value), the net effective fraction of the original base is (A × B) ÷ 100 %.

Insurance Policy Value

Premiums are strictly paid on the insured portion of an asset, which serves as the maximum liability the insurance company bears in case of damage.

questions.question: If x is 15% of y and y is 40% of z, then x + y is ________ % of z.

questions.solution:
Given:

x = 15% of y

y = 40% of z

questions.question: The savings of Radha are equal to 28% of her expenditure. If her income decreases by 5% and her expenditure increases by 2%, then her savings decrease by:
questions.questionHtml: The savings of Radha are equal to 28% of her expenditure. If her income decreases by 5% and her expenditure increases by 2%, then her savings decrease by:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Expenditure = 100, then Savings = 28, and Income = 100 + 28 = 128.

Change in Income = −5% of 128 = −6.4

Change in Expenditure = +2% of 100 = +2

Change in Savings = Change in Income − Change in Expenditure = −6.4 − (+2) = −8.4

Percentage decrease in Savings = (8.4 ÷ 28) × 100 = 30%.

∴ The correct answer is 30%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Savings = 28% of Expenditure

Income decreases by 5%, Expenditure increases by 2%

Formula Used:

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Change = (Change ÷ Initial Value) × 100

Calculations:

Let the initial expenditure be 100.

⇒ Initial Savings = 28% of 100 = 28

⇒ Initial Income = 100 + 28 = 128

Calculating the changes:

⇒ Income decreases by 5%

⇒ New Income = 128 − (5% of 128) = 128 − 6.4 = 121.6

⇒ Expenditure increases by 2%

⇒ New Expenditure = 100 + (2% of 100) = 102

Finding final savings and percentage change:

⇒ New Savings = New Income − New Expenditure

⇒ New Savings = 121.6 − 102 = 19.6

⇒ Decrease in Savings = 28 − 19.6 = 8.4

⇒ % Decrease = (8.4 ÷ 28) × 100

⇒ % Decrease = (3 ÷ 10) × 100 = 30%

∴ The correct answer is 30%.

Additional Information

Income, Expenditure & Savings

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. Any change in income directly affects expenditure and savings proportionately based on their share.

Percentage Change

Percentage Change = (New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value × 100. A positive result indicates an increase, while a negative result signifies a decrease.

Net Change Method

Instead of calculating final absolute values, we can directly compute the final change by using the mathematical relation: Change in Income = Change in Expenditure + Change in Savings.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 10 km/h. The speed of the stream is 2 km/h. What is the total distance that the boat will travel if it is rowed for 4 hours upstream and 3 hours downstream?
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a boat in still water is 10 km/h. The speed of the stream is 2 km/h. What is the total distance that the boat will travel if it is rowed for 4 hours upstream and 3 hours downstream?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Upstream Speed = 10 − 2 = 8 km/h and Downstream Speed = 10 + 2 = 12 km/h.

Total Distance = (Upstream Speed × Upstream Time) + (Downstream Speed × Downstream Time)

Total Distance = (8 × 4) + (12 × 3) = 32 + 36 = 68 km.

∴ The correct answer is 68 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Speed of boat in still water = 10 km/h

⇒ Speed of stream = 2 km/h

⇒ Time taken upstream = 4 hours

⇒ Time taken downstream = 3 hours

Formulas Used:

⇒ Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of stream

⇒ Downstream Speed = Speed of boat + Speed of stream

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Upstream Speed = 10 − 2 = 8 km/h

⇒ Downstream Speed = 10 + 2 = 12 km/h

⇒ Distance traveled upstream = 8 × 4 = 32 km

⇒ Distance traveled downstream = 12 × 3 = 36 km

⇒ Total Distance = 32 + 36 = 68 km

∴ The correct answer is 68 km.

Additional Information

Speed of Boat in Still Water

If downstream and upstream speeds are given, then Boat Speed = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

If downstream and upstream speeds are given, then Stream Speed = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a boat travels equal distances upstream and downstream, the Average Speed = (Upstream Speed × Downstream Speed) ÷ Boat Speed in still water.

⇒ The ratio of their incomes A : B : C = 88x : 80x : 100x

⇒ Dividing by the common factor 4x, we get:

⇒ A : B : C = 22 : 20 : 25

∴ The correct answer is 22 : 20 : 25.

Additional Information

Combining Ratios

If A : B = m : n and B : C = p : q, the combined ratio A : B : C can be found by making the common term B equal, resulting in (m × p) : (n × p) : (n × q).

Percentage to Ratio Conversion

questions.question: Suresh and Naresh can do a piece of work in 12 and 15 days, respectively. If they started working alternatively for every 1 day and if the work is started by Suresh, how many days will they take to complete 75% of the work?
questions.questionHtml: Suresh and Naresh can do a piece of work in 12 and 15 days, respectively. If they started working alternatively for every 1 day and if the work is started by Suresh, how many days will they take to complete 75% of the work?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Work = LCM(12, 15) = 60 units.

Target Work = 75% of 60 = 45 units.

Work done in a 2-day cycle (Suresh + Naresh) = 5 + 4 = 9 units.

Total time for 45 units = (45 ÷ 9) × 2 = 10 days.

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Suresh = 12 days

Time taken by Naresh = 15 days

Work to be completed = 75% of the total work

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
Suresh 12 60 5
Naresh 15 4

Calculations:

⇒ Target work to be completed = 75% of 60 = 45 units

⇒ Since they work on alternate days starting with Suresh:

⇒ Work done on Day 1 (by Suresh) = 5 units

⇒ Work done on Day 2 (by Naresh) = 4 units

⇒ Work done in 1 cycle (2 days) = 5 + 4 = 9 units

⇒ Number of cycles required to complete 45 units = 45 ÷ 9 = 5 cycles

⇒ Total time taken = 5 cycles × 2 days/cycle = 10 days

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Additional Information

Alternate Days Concept

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the combined work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and determine how many cycles fit into the total work.

Work & Efficiency Relationship

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken when the total work remains constant.

questions.question: S is a point on side PQ of a triangle PQR such that RS = PS = QS. If ∠QPR = 15°, then the value of (2 ∠PQR - ∠PRQ) is:
questions.questionHtml: S is a point on side PQ of a triangle PQR such  that RS = PS = QS. If ∠QPR = 15°, then the value of (2 ∠PQR - ∠PRQ) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since point S lies on PQ and PS = QS, S is the midpoint of side PQ.

Given RS = PS = QS, S acts as the circumcenter of ΔPQR, making PQ the diameter of the circumcircle.

The angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is a right angle, so ∠PRQ = 90°.

Using the angle sum property in ΔPQR: ∠PQR = 180° − 90° − 15° = 75°.

The required value is (2 ∠PQR − ∠PRQ) = 2(75°) − 90° = 150° − 90° = 60°.

∴ The correct answer is 60°.

Alternate Method

Given:

S is a point on side PQ.

RS = PS = QS

∠QPR = 15°

Formula Used:

Angles opposite to equal sides of a triangle are equal.

Sum of interior angles of a triangle = 180°

Calculations:

⇒ In ΔPRS, since PS = RS, the angles opposite to them will be equal.

⇒ ∴ ∠SRP = ∠SPR = 15°

⇒ In ΔQRS, since QS = RS, the angles opposite to them will be equal.

⇒ Let ∠SQR = ∠SRQ = x

⇒ Now, considering the larger ΔPQR, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠QPR + ∠PQR + ∠PRQ = 180°

⇒ 15° + x + (∠SRP + ∠SRQ) = 180°

⇒ 15° + x + (15° + x) = 180°

⇒ 30° + 2x = 180°

⇒ 2x = 150°

⇒ x = 75°

⇒ Therefore, ∠PQR = 75°

⇒ And ∠PRQ = ∠SRP + ∠SRQ = 15° + 75° = 90°

⇒ Value to find: (2 ∠PQR − ∠PRQ)

⇒ (2 × 75°) − 90° = 150° − 90° = 60°

∴ The correct answer is 60°.

Additional Information

Circumcenter of a Right-Angled Triangle

The circumcenter of any right-angled triangle always lies exactly at the midpoint of its hypotenuse. The median to the hypotenuse is exactly half the length of the hypotenuse.

Angle in a Semicircle

By Thales's theorem, an angle subtended by a diameter of a circle at any point on its circumference is always a right angle (90°).

Isosceles Triangle Theorem

If two sides of a triangle are equal, then the angles opposite to those sides are also equal. Conversely, if two angles are equal, the sides opposite to them must be equal.

questions.question: The difference between the semi-perimeter and the sides of ΔABC are 18 cm, 17 cm and 25 cm, respectively. Find the area of the triangle.
questions.questionHtml: The difference between the semi-perimeter and the sides of ΔABC are 18 cm, 17 cm and 25 cm, respectively. Find the area of the triangle.

options.html: 330\(\sqrt{510} \) cm2.
30\(\sqrt{510} \) cm2.
30\(\sqrt{6} \) cm2.

questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given the differences of the semi-perimeter and sides: (s − a) = 18, (s − b) = 17, and (s − c) = 25.

We know that the sum of these differences always equals the semi-perimeter (s).

⇒ s = 18 + 17 + 25 = 60 cm.

Using Heron's formula directly: Area = √[s × (s − a) × (s − b) × (s − c)]

⇒ Area = √[60 × 18 × 17 × 25] = √(459000) = 30√510 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 30√510 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Differences between the semi-perimeter and the sides of a triangle are:

(s − a) = 18 cm

(s − b) = 17 cm

(s − c) = 25 cm

Formula Used:

Semi-perimeter of a triangle, s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2 ⇒ 2s = a + b + c

Area of triangle by Heron's formula = √[s × (s − a) × (s − b) × (s − c)]

Calculations:

⇒ (s − a) + (s − b) + (s − c) = 18 + 17 + 25

⇒ 3s − (a + b + c) = 60

⇒ 3s − 2s = 60

⇒ s = 60 cm

Now, substitute the value of s into Heron's formula:

⇒ Area = √[60 × 18 × 17 × 25]

⇒ Area = √[(4 × 15) × (9 × 2) × 17 × 25]

⇒ Area = √[(4 × 9 × 25) × (15 × 2 × 17)]

⇒ Area = √[900 × 510]

⇒ Area = 30√510 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 30√510 cm2.

Additional Information

Heron's Formula

Used to find the area of a scalene triangle when all three sides are known: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s is the semi-perimeter.

Inradius of a Triangle

The radius (r) of the inscribed circle can be found using the direct relation: r = Area ÷ s.

Equilateral Triangle Area

If all sides of a triangle are equal (a = b = c), the area simplifies to (√3 ÷ 4) × a2.

questions.question: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹80,000 at the same rate of interest per annum for 2 years is ₹98. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.questionHtml: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹80,000 at the same rate of interest per annum for 2 years is ₹98. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is calculated directly using the formula: Difference = P × (R / 100)2

⇒ 98 = 80000 × (R / 100)2

⇒ R2 = (98 × 10000) ÷ 80000

⇒ R2 = 98 ÷ 8 = 12.25

⇒ R = √12.25 = 3.5% = 3½%

∴ The correct answer is 3½%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹80,000

Time (T) = 2 years

Difference between CI and SI (D) = ₹98

Let the rate of interest be R% per annum.

Formula Used:

Difference (D) = P × (R / 100)2

Calculations:

⇒ 98 = 80000 × (R / 100)2

⇒ 98 = 80000 × (R2 / 10000)

⇒ 98 = 8 × R2

⇒ R2 = 98 ÷ 8

⇒ R2 = 49 ÷ 4

⇒ R = √(49 ÷ 4)

⇒ R = 7 ÷ 2

⇒ R = 3.5% or 3½%

∴ The correct answer is 3½%.

Additional Information

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for 3 years is calculated using the formula: D = P × (R / 100)2 × (300 + R) ÷ 100.

Effective Rate for 2 years

The effective compound interest rate for 2 years at R% per annum is (2R + R2 ÷ 100)%. The effective simple interest rate is 2R%. The difference is (R2 ÷ 100)% of the principal.

Tree Method for Compound Interest

In the tree method, the second year's CI includes the interest on the principal plus the interest on the first year's interest. This interest on interest is exactly the difference between CI and SI for 2 years.

questions.question: 5 men and 3 women can earn ₹ 8,400 in 4 days. 9 men and 7 women can earn ₹ 28,700 in 7 days. In how many days will 8 men and 5 women earn ₹ 30,600?
questions.questionHtml: 5 men and 3 women can earn ₹8,400 in 4 days. 9 men and 7 women can earn ₹28,700 in 7 days. In how many days will 8 men and 5 women earn ₹30,600?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

1 day earning of 5M + 3W = 8400 ÷ 4 = ₹2100   ... (i)

1 day earning of 9M + 7W = 28700 ÷ 7 = ₹4100   ... (ii)

Solve (i) × 7 − (ii) × 3: (35M + 21W) − (27M + 21W) = 14700 − 12300

8M = 2400 ⇒ M = ₹300, and substituting M gives W = ₹200.

Daily earning of 8M + 5W = 8(300) + 5(200) = ₹3400.

Total days to earn ₹30600 = 30600 ÷ 3400 = 9 days.

∴ The correct answer is 9 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Earning of 5 men and 3 women in 4 days = ₹8,400

Earning of 9 men and 7 women in 7 days = ₹28,700

Calculations:

Let the daily earning of 1 man be M and 1 woman be W.

⇒ (5M + 3W) × 4 = 8400

⇒ 5M + 3W = 2100   ---- (Equation 1)

⇒ (9M + 7W) × 7 = 28700

⇒ 9M + 7W = 4100   ---- (Equation 2)

Multiplying Equation 1 by 7 and Equation 2 by 3:

⇒ 35M + 21W = 14700   ---- (Equation 3)

⇒ 27M + 21W = 12300   ---- (Equation 4)

Subtracting Equation 4 from Equation 3:

⇒ 35M − 27M = 14700 − 12300

⇒ 8M = 2400

⇒ M = 300

Substitute M = 300 in Equation 1:

⇒ 5(300) + 3W = 2100

⇒ 1500 + 3W = 2100

⇒ 3W = 600

⇒ W = 200

Calculate the daily earning of 8 men and 5 women:

⇒ 8M + 5W = 8(300) + 5(200)

⇒ Total daily earning = 2400 + 1000 = ₹3400

Number of days required to earn ₹30,600:

⇒ Required Days = Total Target Earning ÷ Daily Earning

⇒ Required Days = 30600 ÷ 3400 = 9 days

∴ The correct answer is 9 days.

Additional Information

Work & Wages Rule

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the work done by individuals. When individuals work for the same number of days, their total wages are shared in the ratio of their daily efficiencies or one-day earnings.

Simultaneous Linear Equations

For a system of two variables, equations can be solved by scaling one or both equations to equalize the coefficients of one variable, then adding or subtracting to eliminate it and solve for the remaining unknown.

Unitary Method Application

The fastest way to equate different groups working for different time periods is to calculate the earnings or work done for exactly 1 unit of time (1 day) to establish a common proportional base.

questions.question: When the elevation of the sun changes from 45º to 30º, the shadow of the tower changes by 20 m. Find the height of the tower.
questions.questionHtml: When the elevation of the sun changes from 45º to 30º, the shadow of the tower changes by 20 m. Find the height of the tower.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Distance (d) between two shadow points is given by: d = h(cot θ2 − cot θ1)

Given, d = 20 m, θ1 = 45°, and θ2 = 30°

⇒ 20 = h(cot 30° − cot 45°) = h(√3 − 1)

⇒ h = 20 ÷ (√3 − 1)

⇒ h = [20(√3 + 1)] ÷ 2 = 10(√3 + 1) m

∴ The correct answer is 10(√3 + 1) m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Change in sun's elevation = 45° to 30°

Change in length of shadow (CD) = 20 m

Let AB = h be the height of the tower and BC = x be the initial shadow length.

Calculations:

In right-angled ΔABC,

⇒ tan 45° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ 1 = h ÷ x

⇒ x = h

In right-angled ΔABD,

⇒ tan 30° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ 1 ÷ √3 = h ÷ (x + 20)

⇒ x + 20 = h√3

Substitute x = h into the equation:

⇒ h + 20 = h√3

⇒ h√3 − h = 20

⇒ h(√3 − 1) = 20

⇒ h = 20 ÷ (√3 − 1)

Rationalising the denominator by multiplying the numerator and denominator by (√3 + 1):

⇒ h = [20 × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1)(√3 + 1)]

⇒ h = 20(√3 + 1) ÷ (3 − 1)

⇒ h = 20(√3 + 1) ÷ 2

⇒ h = 10(√3 + 1) m

∴ The correct answer is 10(√3 + 1) m.

Additional Information

Angle of Elevation

It is the angle formed between the horizontal line of sight and the object when the observer looks upwards.

Important Trigonometric Values

For height and distance problems, remember these values: tan 30° = 1 ÷ √3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

Rationalisation

To remove surds from the denominator like (a − √b), multiply both numerator and denominator by its conjugate (a + √b) to create a rational base.

questions.question: Two pipes fill a tank when working individually in 25 and 40 hours, respectively while a third pipe can drain the filled tank in 16 hours. If all the three pipes are turned on at the same time when the tank is empty, how long will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.questionHtml: Two pipes fill a tank when working individually in 25 and 40 hours, respectively while a third pipe can drain the filled tank in 16 hours. If all the three pipes are turned on at the same time when the tank is empty, how long will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Work = LCM (25, 40, 16) = 400 units.

Individual efficiencies: A = 16, B = 10, C = −25 units/hr.

Net efficiency (A+B+C) = 16 + 10 − 25 = 1 unit/hr.

Time required = 400 ÷ 1 = 400 hours.

400 hours = (384 + 16) hours = 16 days 16 hours.

∴ The correct answer is 16 days 16 hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by Pipe A = 25 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 40 hours

Time taken by Pipe C (outlet) = 16 hours

Formula Used:

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

Pipes Time Capacity Efficiency
Pipe A 25
400
 16
Pipe B 40 10
Pipe C 16 −25

Calculations:

⇒ Total capacity = LCM (25, 40, 16) = 400 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of (A + B + C) = 16 + 10 − 25 = 1 unit/hr

⇒ Total time taken = 400 ÷ 1 = 400 hours

⇒ To convert hours into days: 400 ÷ 24 = 16 days and 16 hours (since 24 × 16 = 384)

∴ The correct answer is 16 days 16 hours.

Additional Information

Negative Work in Pipes

An outlet pipe (leak) performs negative work. While calculating combined efficiency, subtract the rate of the outlet pipe from the rate of the inlet pipes.

LCM Method

Total capacity is assumed as the LCM of individual times taken. Individual efficiency = Total capacity ÷ Individual time.

Time Conversion

To convert hours into days, divide by 24. For example, 400 hours = 400 ÷ 24 = 16 days and 16 hours remainder.

questions.question: A mother is currently twice as old as her daughter. 20 years ago, the age of the mother was 12 times the age of daughter. The present age of the mother in year is _______.
questions.questionHtml: A mother is currently twice as old as her daughter. 20 years ago, the age of the mother was 12 times the age of daughter. The present age of the mother in year is _______.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Present ratio (M : D) = 2 : 1 (Difference = 1 part) and 20 years ago ratio = 12 : 1 (Difference = 11 parts).

Equate the difference by multiplying the Present ratio by 11 → New Present Ratio = 22 : 11

Decrease in ratio parts = 22 − 12 = 10 parts ≡ 20 years → 1 part = 2 years.

Mother's present age = 22 parts × 2 = 44 years.

∴ The correct answer is 44 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Present age of Mother is twice her daughter's age.

20 years ago, the Mother was 12 times her daughter's age.

Calculation:

Let the present age of the daughter be x years.

⇒ Present age of the mother = 2x years

20 years ago:

⇒ Daughter's age = (x − 20) years

⇒ Mother's age = (2x − 20) years

According to the given condition:

⇒ 2x − 20 = 12 × (x − 20)

⇒ 2x − 20 = 12x − 240

⇒ 12x − 2x = 240 − 20

⇒ 10x = 220

⇒ x = 22

Present age of the mother = 2x = 2 × 22 = 44 years.

∴ The correct answer is 44 years.

Additional Information

Constant Age Difference Concept

The difference between the ages of any two people always remains constant, whether it is past, present, or future.

Cross-Multiplication Method

If the ratio of ages changes from a:b to c:d after T years, the equations can be directly solved using the ratio equalization method or cross-product differences.

Ratio of Ages in Future/Past

If present ages are x and y, their ages 'n' years ago were (x − n) and (y − n), and after 'n' years will be (x + n) and (y + n).

questions.question: A shopkeeper offered following four different discount schemes for buyers on an item. A. Two successive discounts of 8%. B. A discount of 11% followed by a discount of 5%. C. Successive discounts of 13% and 3% D. A discount of 16%. Which discount scheme should be opted for getting the item at minimum price?
questions.questionHtml:
A shopkeeper offered following four different discount schemes for buyers on an item.
A. Two successive discounts of 8%.
B. A discount of 11% followed by a discount of 5%.
C. Successive discounts of 13% and 3%
D. A discount of 16%.
Which discount scheme should be opted for getting the item at minimum price?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For successive discounts x% and y%, the effective single discount is [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

When the sum of discounts (x + y) is equal, the effective discount is maximum when the product (x × y) is minimum.

The sum in all schemes is 16%. The products are: A → 64, B → 55, C → 39, D → 0.

Scheme D has the minimum product (0), thus giving the maximum effective discount of 16%.

The maximum discount directly results in the minimum selling price for the buyer.

∴ The correct answer is Scheme D.

Alternate Method

Given:

Four discount schemes for an item:

A. Two successive discounts of 8%.

B. A discount of 11% followed by a discount of 5%.

C. Successive discounts of 13% and 3%.

D. A single discount of 16%.

Formula Used:

Effective discount for successive discounts x% and y% = [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Calculations:

Let the Marked Price (MP) of the item be 100.

⇒ For Scheme A: Effective Discount = 8 + 8 − (8 × 8) ÷ 100 = 16 − 0.64 = 15.36%

⇒ SP for Scheme A = 100 − 15.36 = 84.64

⇒ For Scheme B: Effective Discount = 11 + 5 − (11 × 5) ÷ 100 = 16 − 0.55 = 15.45%

⇒ SP for Scheme B = 100 − 15.45 = 84.55

⇒ For Scheme C: Effective Discount = 13 + 3 − (13 × 3) ÷ 100 = 16 − 0.39 = 15.61%

⇒ SP for Scheme C = 100 − 15.61 = 84.39

⇒ For Scheme D: Single discount is 16%

⇒ SP for Scheme D = 100 − 16 = 84.00

⇒ Comparing all selling prices, Scheme D provides the item at the minimum selling price (84.00).

∴ The correct answer is Scheme D.

Additional Information

Successive Discount Formula

When two discounts of a% and b% are given successively, the equivalent single discount is given by: [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Maximizing Discount Trick

If the sum of two successive discounts is constant, the effective discount is maximized when the difference between the two discount values is maximum (i.e., their product is minimum).

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Marked Price (MP) is the original price tag of the item. Selling Price (SP) is the price after applying the discount. SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: A wire of square shape with an area of 676 cm 2 is bent in the form of a circle. Find the diameter of the circle (in cm).
questions.questionHtml: A wire of square shape with an area of 676 cm2 is bent in the form of a circle. Find the diameter of the circle (in cm).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Side of the square = √676 = 26 cm.

Since the same wire is bent, the Circumference of the circle = Perimeter of the square.

Circumference = 4 × 26 = 104 cm.

Diameter = Circumference ÷ π = (104 × 7) ÷ 22 = 364 ÷ 11 = 33(1/11) cm.

∴ The correct answer is 33(1/11) cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Area of the square shaped wire = 676 cm2

The wire is bent into the form of a circle.

Formula Used:

Area of a square = a2

Perimeter of a square = 4 × a

Circumference of a circle = π × d (where d is the diameter)

Calculations:

⇒ a2 = 676

⇒ a = √676

⇒ a = 26 cm

⇒ Perimeter of the square = 4 × 26 = 104 cm

⇒ Since the same wire is used to form the circle, the circumference of the circle is equal to the perimeter of the square.

⇒ Circumference of the circle = 104 cm

⇒ π × d = 104

⇒ (22 ÷ 7) × d = 104

⇒ d = (104 × 7) ÷ 22

⇒ d = (52 × 7) ÷ 11

⇒ d = 364 ÷ 11

⇒ d = 33(1/11) cm

∴ The correct answer is 33(1/11) cm.

Additional Information

Wire Bending Rule

When a continuous wire is bent from one enclosed 2D shape into another, its total length remains completely unchanged. This directly means the perimeters of both geometric shapes will always be equal.

Area of a Circle vs Square

For a fixed perimeter length, a circle will consistently enclose a significantly larger area than any polygon, including a square. The ratio of the area of a circle to a square having the identical perimeter is roughly 14:11.

Circumference to Diameter Link

The core relationship joining the circumference (C) and diameter (d) of a circle is represented directly as C = πd, where the mathematical constant π equals roughly 22/7 or 3.14.

questions.question: A vertical pole of length 8.3 m casts a shadow of length 4.15 m. Find the height of the tree that casts a 40 m long shadow under similar conditions (in m).
questions.questionHtml: A vertical pole of length 8.3 m casts a shadow of length 4.15 m. Find the height of the tree that casts a 40 m long shadow under similar conditions (in m).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Under similar conditions, the ratio of an object's height to the length of its shadow is constant.

Ratio = Height of Pole ÷ Shadow of Pole = 8.3 ÷ 4.15 = 2

Height of the Tree = Shadow of Tree × Ratio

Height of the Tree = 40 × 2 = 80 m

∴ The correct answer is 80 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height of the pole = 8.3 m

Shadow of the pole = 4.15 m

Shadow of the tree = 40 m

Formula Used:

Since the shadows are cast under similar conditions, the angle of elevation of the sun is the same, forming similar triangles. Therefore:

Height of Object 1 ÷ Shadow of Object 1 = Height of Object 2 ÷ Shadow of Object 2

Calculation:

Let the height of the tree be h m.

⇒ 8.3 ÷ 4.15 = h ÷ 40

⇒ 2 = h ÷ 40

⇒ h = 40 × 2

⇒ h = 80

∴ The correct answer is 80 m.

Additional Information

Properties of Similar Triangles

When two right-angled triangles are formed under the same angle of elevation (such as by sun rays at the same time), they are similar, meaning the ratio of their corresponding sides is always identically equal.

Direct Proportion

The height of a vertical object and the length of its cast shadow are directly proportional. If Height ∝ Shadow, then H1/S1 = H2/S2.

Angle of Elevation

The phrase 'similar conditions' implies that the angle of elevation of the sun is identical for both locations, ensuring the shadow lengths follow the exact same geometric scale as the object heights.

  • It's a complex sentence as one clause is dependent on the other.
  • The subject 'we' performs the action 'hope' and in the second part the subject 'we' performs the action 'shall win' against the object 'the match'.
  • If this sentence is changed to passive voice, then the subject, verb form and object are all changed, in order to retain the meaning of the sentence.
  • So, the object takes the place of the subject and vice versa and the word 'by' is introduced as now the subject receives the action by the object. The verb form of the sentence is also changed from active form to passive.
  • Structure: 
  • "Subject (we) + verb (hope)" will change to "subject (it) + verb (is hoped)"

​                                                                  and

  • "Subject (We) + verb (shall win) + object (the match)" changes to "New subject (the match) + verb (will be won) + by + new object (us)"
  • 'That' is the conjunction that joins these two clauses.
  • The passive form of 'hope' in the simple present tense is 'is hoped' and 'shall win' is 'will be won'.
  • So the correct answer is Option 1.
     

Correct sentence: It is hoped that the match will be won by us.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) Not only the board of directors refused to acknowledge the validity of the shareholders' grievances / (2) concerning the lack of corporate transparency, / (3) but they also summarily dismissed the proposal to initiate / (4) an independent investigation into the firm’s offshore accounts.

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • The phrase “Not only the board of directors refused to acknowledge...” is incorrect because the construction of “Not only... but also” requires proper parallelism and auxiliary verb usage.

Correct sentence: Not only did the board of directors refuse to acknowledge the validity of the shareholders' grievances concerning the lack of corporate transparency, but they also summarily dismissed the proposal to initiate an independent investigation into the firm’s offshore accounts.

Additional Information

  • Parallelism: In sentences using constructions like “Not only... but also,” it’s important to maintain parallel grammatical structures.
  • Auxiliary Verb Usage: In negative sentences, auxiliary verbs like “did,” “does,” or “do” are required before the main verb.
  • Example:
    • Incorrect: Not only she sings beautifully but also dances gracefully.
    • Correct: Not only does she sing beautifully but also dances gracefully.

questions.question: Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: (1) The synthesis of organic compounds, along with the subsequent analysis of their molecular structures / (2) using high-resolution nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, / (3) provide invaluable insights into the biosynthetic pathways / (4) of rare flora found only in the Amazonian rainforest.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. provide invaluable insights .

Key Points

  • The subject of the sentence, "The synthesis of organic compounds, along with the subsequent analysis of their molecular structures," is singular because it refers to one collective process.
  • The verb "provide" is plural, which creates a subject-verb agreement error. The correct singular verb form should be "provides".
  • The sentence structure needs to ensure that the verb agrees with the singular subject.

Correct sentence: The synthesis of organic compounds, along with the subsequent analysis of their molecular structures, using high-resolution nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, provides invaluable insights into the biosynthetic pathways of rare flora found only in the Amazonian rainforest.

Additional Information

  • Subject-Verb Agreement Rules:
    • A singular subject requires a singular verb (e.g., "He runs").
    • A plural subject requires a plural verb (e.g., "They run").
    • When subjects are joined by "along with," "as well as," or "together with," the verb agrees with the main subject, not the phrase that follows.
  • Examples:
    • Incorrect: The bouquet of flowers smell lovely.
    • Correct: The bouquet of flowers smells lovely.

    • दिए गए वाक्य में 'Inquired' को 'said to' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
    • Conjunction 'Whether' हटा दिया जाएगा।
    • 'his' 'your' में बदल जाएगा। (Indirect to Direct transformation)
    • 'was' को 'is' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
    • अंत में question mark जोड़ा जाएगा।
  • इसलिए, ऊपर बताए गए बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The meals are frequently served in tiny Tupperware containers and are labelled with nutritional information.

B. These services provide individually packaged pre-portioned meals to help people eat a balanced diet.

C. Customers can use these services to cook and prepare meals or get ready-to-eat meals.

D. A meal delivery service delivers fresh or frozen cooked meals to customers' homes or businesses through packaging.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The paragraph introduces the concept of a meal delivery service and explains its features and benefits.
  • Sentence D is the first sentence as it introduces the main topic:
    • "A meal delivery service delivers fresh or frozen cooked meals to customers' homes or businesses through packaging."
  • Sentence A follows as it describes how the meals are packaged and labelled:
    • "The meals are frequently served in tiny Tupperware containers and are labelled with nutritional information."
  • Sentence B is the third sentence because it explains the purpose of these services:
    • "These services provide individually packaged pre-portioned meals to help people eat a balanced diet."
  • Sentence C is the fourth as it provides additional options available to customers:
    • "Customers can use these services to cook and prepare meals or get ready-to-eat meals."

The correct sequence is DABC.

Key Points

  • The idiom "When it rains, it pours" means when something happens, whether good or unpleasant, it typically happens more than once and frequently within a short amount of time.
  • The idiom "When it rains, it pours" is frequently used in English to imply that related events occur one after the other.
  • It can be applied either positively or negatively in a variety of circumstances.

Additional Information

  • An idiom is a phrase that, when read as a whole, has a meaning that cannot be inferred from the individual word meanings.
  • In short, it's the verbal version of using the incorrect mathematical formula and still getting the right answer.
  • An example of an idiom is "kill two birds with one stone".

In this section, each item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given as SI and S6. The middle four sentences in each have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. You are required to find the proper sequence of the four sentences and mark your response accordingly.

S1: Industries would consider the forest as merely a source of raw material for its factories. 
P:  Since these industries have a greater reach than the local people, they are not interested in the sustainability of the forest in one particular area. 
Q: For example, after cutting down all the teak trees in one area, they will get their teak from a forest farther away.
R: They do not have any stake in ensuring that one particular area should yield an optimal amount of produce for all generations to come.  
S: And huge interest-groups lobby the government for access to these raw materials at artificially low rates. 
S6: This is bad for environment and everyone.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "SPQR"

Key Points 

  • The 1st sentence states that Industries would consider the forest as merely a source of raw material
  • Sentence S states how the industries acquire this raw material at low prices.
  • Sentence P states that these industries have a greater reach than the local people and they are not concerned with the deterioration of forest
  • Sentence Q and Sentence R respectively elaborate on the selfishness of the industries towards "forest"
Hence the correct passage: S1: Industries would consider the forest as merely a source of raw material for its factories. S: And huge interest-groups lobby the government for access to these raw materials at artificially low rates. P:  Since these industries have a greater reach than the local people, they are not interested in the sustainability of the forest in one particular area. Q: For example, after cutting down all the teak trees in one area, they will get their teak from a forest farther away. R: They do not have any stake in ensuring that one particular area should yield an optimal amount of produce for all generations to come.

questions.question: Out of the given options, choose the one which is the correct direct speech of the sentence given below. My teacher often says to me that if I don't work hard I shall fail.
questions.questionHtml:
Out of the given options, choose the one which is the correct direct speech of the sentence given below.

My teacher often says to me that if I don't work hard I shall fail.

options.text: My teacher often says to me, “If you didn't work hard, you shall fail.”
options.html: My teacher often says to me, “If you didn't work hard, you shall fail.”

options.html: My teacher often says to me, “If you don't work hard, you will fail.”

options.html: My teacher often says to me, “If you doesn't work hard, you will fail.”

options.text: My teacher often said to me, “If you don't work hard, you will fail.”
options.html: My teacher often said to me, “If you don't work hard, you will fail.”

questions.solution:
The direct speech is My teacher often says to me, “If you don't work hard, you will fail.”

Additional Information

  • Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from direct to indirect speech:
  • When the indirect speech is in an assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
    • The reporting verb 'says to' will remain the same as per the given options.
    • Connector 'that' is replaced by a comma and inverted commas.
    • The tense of indirect/reported speech will remain the same as the reporting verb(says) is in the present tense.
    • The auxiliary verb don't will remain the same as per the pronoun 'you' whereas 'shall' gets converted into 'will' according to the pronoun 'you'.
    • The personal pronouns will be changed according to the subject and object of the reporting verb.
    • ​Here the 1st person 'I' will change into the 2nd person 'you' as per the object.
  • ​At last line up the remaining part.
     

Following these steps, we finally get- My teacher often says to me, “If you don't work hard, you will fail.”

Additional Information  ​​​​

  • In the case of a general truth or universal fact, there will be no change in the tense of reported speech.
